anomaly_def.Name: MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Excessive accumulation of obsolete row versions, undo records, and dead index entries that outpaces background cleanup, inflating storage and scan costs.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Mis-tuned engine parameters (memory, checkpointing, parallelism, background workers, etc.) that create artificial resource bottlenecks or disable timely maintenance despite hardware capacity.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Saturation or mismanagement of connection, socket, or network transport resources that delays or interrupts client–server communication and query execution.

When all three root causes coexist, the database exhibits a blended failure signature:  • Version store and table bloat grow rapidly, while autovacuum/vacuum or purge workers remain perpetually behind because configuration limits throttle their throughput.  • Checkpoint storms or overly aggressive WAL flushing amplify I/O pressure, yet actual CPU and disk utilization appear imbalanced due to sub-optimal parameter settings.  • Clients experience intermittent connection timeouts, authentication delays, and prolonged result-set transfers; simultaneously, backend processes pile up in client-read/write and tuple-visibility check waits.  • System views report soaring dead-tuple ratios, rising transaction-ID age, swelling redo/backlog sizes, and a high count of idle-in-transaction sessions holding snapshots open.  • Latency and throughput vary erratically: moments of network congestion or socket exhaustion compound with sudden maintenance bursts, making performance regressions hard to attribute to a single layer.

Causal chain: Misconfigured memory, checkpoint, and worker parameters slow or starve the vacuum/purge subsystem, allowing MVCC debris to accumulate. The bloated data footprint increases I/O volume and stretches transaction-commit and query-execution times, keeping sessions open longer. Prolonged session lifetimes enlarge the active connection pool, consuming more server processes/threads and sockets. This raises pressure on the listener backlog and network stack, producing connection stalls and retransmissions that further elongate transactions. The resulting feedback loop—sluggish cleanup ➝ heap/index bloat ➝ longer queries ➝ extended and additional connections ➝ network and listener saturation—magnifies both the storage-level visibility overhead and the parameter-induced resource mismatch, ultimately degrading OLTP responsiveness and risking transaction-wraparound or outage.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with connection establishment, authentication exchange, protocol correctness, network reachability, or client/server communication stability.
entry.solution_guidance: Check endpoint reachability, authentication flow, connection limits, protocol compatibility, transport stability, and client connection lifecycle management.
